full_instruction: Write a comedy story about a kid whose coding class presentation slides accidentally pull up his browser history instead of his project, told in dialogue between him and his very calm teacher. During the story, reveal that the embarrassing tab was just forty open tutorials on how to fix the exact bug he's currently presenting about. End with the class actually applauding because the tabs prove he did the work.

text: "Ms. Halloway, my slides are haunted by a browser history theme called 'My Entire Digital Existence' instead of showing my cookie jar project!" I cried as the screen displayed photos of hamsters wearing tuxedos. "Just hit F5!" I begged frantically, desperate to clear the chaotic mess before everyone saw that my search for 'how to hide homework' was definitely not supposed to be there. She sipped her tea calmly and noted that while Slide 12 still played a cat falling off a couch, those embarrassing tabs were actually just forty open tutorials on how to fix the exact bug I'm currently presenting about. "But why does the graph look so steep?" she asked, ignoring my panic about the frog pajama pants visible in the corner. "Perhaps," she smiled, "your project is finally optimized to reveal that you've been practicing this fix for weeks." The class suddenly erupted in applause, realizing the 'accidental' history proved he had actually done the work.

During the story, reveal that his freestyled ideas are somehow better than anything he actually prepared. Include the exact sentence "The mirror never talks back." End with him winning specifically because of the part he made up on the spot.

text: Leo stared into the polished chrome of his bedroom dresser, reciting his rehearsed speech for the twenty-first time since breakfast. The moment he stepped onto the podium, however, a sudden panic caused every single note card to vanish from his mind like smoke in a breeze. As the silence stretched, Leo began freestyling policy ideas that were far more brilliant and chaotic than anything written on the cards he had prepared. "The mirror never talks back," he muttered to himself as he improvised a solution to traffic using imaginary teleportation gates, completely outshining his original plan. The students erupted in laughter and applause, realizing instantly that his spontaneous genius was superior to the stiff, forgotten script. In the end, Leo secured the presidency not despite forgetting his notes, but specifically because of the brilliant nonsense he made up on the spot.

text: Leo practiced his class president speech in front of the mirror at least twenty times, memorizing every dull point about recycling until the words felt stale, only for him to forget his notes on stage and panic while the mirror never talks back. Instead of freezing, he improvised wild ideas like turning the library into a laser tag arena and declaring recess the supreme law, discovering that his spontaneous ramblings were infinitely more exciting than the dry scripts he had rehearsed. The crowd roared with laughter and genuine enthusiasm at his creative vision, proving that his genuine passion far surpassed the robotic perfection of his preparation. Mrs. Gable smiled warmly as she watched him lead the class with an energy no amount of memorization could ever achieve, and by the time he walked off stage, he knew his freestyle had saved the election. The vote tally was announced moments later, revealing that Leo won specifically because of the part he made up on the spot, securing victory with the very ideas he hadn't planned to say.

text: Leo slumped over his desk, muttering about torque ratios while half the class secretly recorded his rambling speech for two full minutes. His sleepy voice drifted through the quiet library, declaring that his autonomous bot would surely win because it had "super-duper legs." I tried to cover my mouth, but Leo's dream logic kept escalating, describing a battle where the robot fought off a giant hamster made of cheese. The teacher finally stepped out from behind her stack of books, looking at the live stream on her tablet with a mix of amusement and confusion. She gently shook his shoulder and asked, "Hey, buddy, did your robot ever make it home?" Leo jumped awake, blushing furiously as he realized everyone had been listening to his sleep talk about imaginary wins.

text: When Mr. Henderson walked in with a clipboard full of disciplinary warnings, the class immediately started scribbling frantic Xs on their secret bingo cards for squares like "brings snacks" and "can't pronounce a single name." They had spent three weeks perfecting their timing to ensure every substitute triggered a game-ending win, unaware that this particular visitor was actually the AP's cousin sent specifically to catch them red-handed. As the teacher demanded strict silence, a student whispered about feeling an overwhelming surge of free space energy vibrating through the room, signaling that their conspiracy had been discovered. Panic rippled through the group until they realized the substitute wasn't writing notes in his book but instead was eagerly drawing a line across a "wears khakis" square on his own card. Instead of turning them in for insubordination, the substitute laughed and declared he wanted to play along with their ridiculous bingo tradition after all. With the class cheering wildly, the AP's cousin officially joined the game, promising that next time he would try to get a "makes weird jokes" before calling out a winner.

text: When the red strobe lights erupted like a crimson sun over the battlefield of Room 304, the exam proctor screamed, "All units to the breach!" in a voice that could shatter glass. A lone soldier named Kevin remained a stubborn casualty, his Scantron sheet bubbling with existential dread as he refused to surrender to the chaos. The instructor was forced to drag this insubordinate casualty out of the trenches and into the hallway while the rest of the platoon scrambled for cover behind their desks. As the class huddled in the stairwell, they watched Kevin frantically try to fill in answer bubbles on his way to safety. Once the all-clear sounded, the entire squad unanimously declared these ten minutes the single most stressful casualty of the entire semester.
